n: Isaiah bursts into praise: the Lord is his God, who has done wonders and carried out long-planned purposes with perfect faithfulness.
God has turned a proud, fortified city into a heap of rubble, never to be rebuilt. This “city” stands for all the world’s organized wickedness.
So even strong and ruthless nations will honor and revere God.
God has been a fortress for the poor and needy in distress, a shelter from storms and shade from scorching heat, when the ruthless rage like a storm against a wall.
As a cloud’s shadow cools desert heat, God silences the uproar of foreigners and the song of tyrants.

On this mountain — Zion — the Lord will prepare a rich banquet for all peoples, with the finest food and aged wine. This anticipates the messianic feast; Latter-day scripture speaks of the “supper of the Lord” prepared for all nations.

f.g: Aged wine, left to mature on its sediment.

n: On this mountain He will remove the shroud of mourning and the veil of spiritual blindness covering all nations.

f.w: the veil that is spread over all nations

f.g: A burial shroud or veil of grief.

n: He will swallow up death forever and wipe away tears from every face, removing His people’s disgrace. Paul and John quote this; it is fulfilled through Christ’s Resurrection.

f.w: He will swallow up death in victory
wipe away tears from off all faces

n: In that day people will say: “This is our God! We waited for Him, and He saved us. Let us rejoice in His salvation.”
The Lord’s hand will rest protectively on Zion, but Moab — here a symbol of proud enemies — will be trampled like straw in a manure pit.
Moab will flail like a drowning swimmer trying to stay afloat, but God will bring down its pride and its skillful schemes.

f.g: Moab struggles helplessly in the dung pit.

n: God will bring down Moab’s high fortified walls and level them to the dust.

f.w: bring to the ground, even to the dust
